children: Here's a list of key deals reported across sectors this week:
Edgewise Therapeutics
jumped 12% at least partly amid a report that the biopharmaceutical firm has attracted takeover interest. Edgewise
is speculated to have hired advisers to run a sales process, according to traders, who cited a Betaville “uncooked” alert that was circulating on Friday.
Palo Alto Networks

is reportedly in talks to acquire Israeli AI security startup Clutch Security for about $500M. Discussions are ongoing and may not lead to a deal, the report said. Clutch develops software that helps companies track passwords and authentication codes used by AI agents.
Rhythm Pharmaceuticals
surged 22% after a report that AstraZeneca
made an almost $10 billion offer for the biotech company. The UK pharmaceutical behemoth offered $124 a share for Rhythm
last month, according to a media report.
Meta Platforms
is buying artificial intelligence coding startup Conductor, Axios reported. Conductor, which was founded in 2024, allows software engineers to manage multiple coding agents simultaneously.
Eagle Nuclear Energy
said pre-market Wednesday it signed a binding letter of intent to
Noble Plains Uranium
in an all-stock transaction that values Noble Plains at C$0.125/share, based on an exchange rate of 0.0167 Eagle share per Noble Plains share.
MTY Group jumped 14% after it was disclosed that restaurant operator Foodtastic Inc. had offered to purchase the Canadian franchisor for about C$1 billion ($720 million).
Organigram Global
on Tuesday agreed to acquire its domestic rival Aurora Cannabis
in a cash and stock deal worth roughly C$561M after months of a hostile takeover campaign by its U.S. competitor Curaleaf Holdings
Salesforce

announced it signed a definitive agreement to purchase Cresta, a voice-first operating system for customer experience. Terms weren't disclosed. The deal is expected to close in Q1 of fiscal year 2028.
Marvell Technology
disclosed on Monday that it intends to acquire Lumentum
in an all-stock deal.
